chunks: Muhammad ibn Ja'far Al-Qurashi Al-Kufi Al-Razzaz narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazee', from Salih ibn Uqbah, from Yazid ibn Abd al-Malik, who said:

I was with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) when a group of people passed by riding on donkeys. He asked, 'Where are these going?' I said, 'To the graves of the martyrs.' He said, 'What prevents them from visiting the lone Martyr?'

A man from the Iraqis asked, 'Is his visitation obligatory?' He said, 'His visitation is better than one Hajj and one Umrah,' until he counted twenty Hajjs and twenty Umrahs. Then he said, 'Purified and accepted.'

He said, 'By Allah, I did not rise from his presence until a man came to him and said to him, 'I have performed Hajj, 'I have performed nineteen Hajjs. Please pray to Allah that He grants me the completion of the twentieth.'
He asked, 'Have you visited the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him)?' He said, 'No.' He said, 'Verily, his visitation is better than twenty Hajjs.'

key_terms.الشَّهِيد الْغَرِيب: The lone/abandoned Martyr (referring to Imam al-Husayn)
key_terms.زِيَارَة: Visitation (of the graves of the Imams and martyrs)
key_terms.مَبْرُورَات: Purified/accepted (referring to accepted acts of worship)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting the grave of Imam al-Husayn compared to Hajj?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) elevates the status of Imam al-Husayn (a.s.) as the 'Gharib' (Stranger) among the martyrs, distinguishing his grave visitation from general martyr cemeteries. The Imam quantifies this spiritual merit as surpassing twenty accepted Hajjs and Umrahs, a specific reward underscored by the anecdote of a pilgrim who had completed nineteen Hajjs, illustrating the cumulative value of this singular act of devotion in Shia piety.
